results.hypothesis: To determine whether applying demographic parity versus equal opportunity fairness constraints to a credit approval model results in significantly different rejection patterns for male applicants when overall accuracy is held constant.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Baseline model without fairness constraints trained on the same dataset
results.success_criteria: Supporting the hypothesis: Demographic parity leads to higher rejection rate among male applicants compared to equal opportunity when overall accuracy is controlled. Refuting the hypothesis: No significant difference in male rejection rates between the two fairness constraints.
results.notes: Hypothesis supported: Demographic parity resulted in higher rejection rate (0.780) for male applicants compared to equal opportunity (0.724), with a difference of 0.057.
